subject: Coordination: tailored incident notice & limited scope for Oakridge data exposures
messages:
From: Jared Cole <security@oakridgepayments.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lynn Park <legal@oakridgepayments.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential exposure — initial notification ask

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this quickly. We saw anomalous access in a customer bucket that maps to a limited set of Redwood API keys used by a partner integration. At this point our internal triage suggests a scoped exposure (customer IDs and hashed tokens) for approximately 3% of transactions over a 36-hour window.

Before we escalate to our legal team, we wanted to align on Redwood's incident notification obligations and what evidence you can provide (logs, timelines, proof of remediation). Specifically:
- What notification window does Redwood expect under your DPA for limited, scoped exposures?
- Can you confirm whether subprocessors that handled the affected workloads will be available for forensics or whether evidence will be produced via Redwood only?
- Preferred secure channel for evidence handoff (S3 presigned, encrypted transfer, or shared forensic environment)?

Appreciate a quick ack. Our procurement/legal folks will need to restate this in contract redlines if we move forward.

Thanks,
Jared Cole
Head of Security, Oakridge Payments
attachments: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <security@oakridgepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure — initial notification ask

Jared — thanks for flagging this and for the early details. Quick ack: we received the alert and will prioritize. High-level responses below; we can lock specifics in a short call.

1) Notification window: Our standard DPA baseline is 72 hours from confirmation of a security incident that materially impacts Customer Data. For very narrow, non-material exposures (limited scope, transient access), we can agree contractually to a staged notification approach — preliminary notification within 24 hours of confirmation, followed by a 72-hour detailed window for evidence and remediation steps.

2) Subprocessor forensics: Redwood will be the primary evidence custodian. We do work with subprocessors (e.g., telemetry and logging providers) under flow-down obligations; however, direct access to subprocessor environments is usually restricted. We can coordinate mediated access where necessary or provide signed forensic exports (logs, snapshots). We typically avoid giving customers direct subproc log access because of cross-tenant telemetry and privacy concerns.

3) Evidence handoff: Preferred is an encrypted S3 presigned transfer with limited TTL. We can also host a temporary, access-scoped forensic workspace on our secure environment and provide audit logs for access.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal) and Ben (ops) to propose concrete clause language and the evidence transfer method. Can we get a 30-min sync today or tomorrow?

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Potential exposure — initial notification ask (proposed redline)

Jared / Naomi / Ben — attaching a redline to propose contractual language that balances Oakridge's desire for prompt notice with Redwood's operational and privacy constraints. Key points in the attached redline (oakridge_clause_redline.docx):

- Staged notice: preliminary acknowledgement within 24 hours of confirmation, substantive notification (including root cause, impacted data classes, and remediation plan) within 72 hours.
- Scoped disclosure: Redwood will identify affected Customer Data categories and affected customer IDs; we will not provide raw telemetry that contains unrelated third-party data.
- Subprocessor engagement: Where evidence requires subprocessor exports, Redwood will coordinate production with reasonable assistance; Redwood will either (a) produce verified forensic exports signed by Redwood and the subprocessor, or (b) provide a secured, mediated view into the subprocessor's exported artifacts. Direct customer access to subprocessor environments is excluded.
- Evidence retention & transfer: Forensics artifacts will be made available for 90 days in a secured transfer location. Transfers will use encryption-in-transit and at-rest; presigned S3 with short TTL is acceptable.

Please review the redline. Jared — if you need narrower timelines (48h instead of 72h) note that will likely require an SLA uplift and procurement approval (we can scope that in the order form).

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Potential exposure — initial notification ask (ops details)

Jared — quick operational clarifications from my side:

- Scope confirmation: We'll run a targeted telemetry sweep to confirm the exact keys/traces. Expect an initial scope confirmation within 8 hours of our confirmation call.
- Subprocessor list: The affected integration path touches a log-aggregation subprocessor and a managed caching layer. I'll provide a roster and contract status in the sync.
- Evidence format: We can supply zipped log bundles (sha256 checksummed) and an index file mapping to event timestamps. For extremely sensitive items we propose an escrowed read-only S3 bucket with monitored access (instructions attached: s3_transfer_instructions.txt).

One operational ask: to keep the investigation narrow, please share a list of sample customer IDs or transaction IDs you believe are affected. That will avoid broad data pulls and reduce privacy exposure.

If Oakridge needs a contractual promise for expedited notice (<72h), we can support it as an add-on with defined cost and a dedicated on-call ops allocation.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Incident Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Potential exposure — initial notification ask (next steps)

Jared — thanks everyone for the quick coordination. Confirming next steps so the contract team has a clean record:

1) Redwood will send a redline (attached) to Oakridge legal proposing staged notice: 24h ack + 72h substantive.
2) Ops (Ben) will deliver an initial scope confirmation within 8 hours of our joint confirmation call; full forensic bundle available within 72 hours after substantive confirmation.
3) Evidence transfer method: presigned S3 with 48-hour TTL by default; escrowed read-only bucket available as an upgrade. All artifacts will be checksummed and include a manifest.
4) Subprocessors: Redwood will coordinate subprocessor-exported artifacts and will provide signed forensic exports; direct subprocessor console access is excluded.

Please confirm acceptance of the staging approach and whether Oakridge needs the 48-hour SLA instead of 72 hours (note procurement implications). If accepted, Marissa will incorporate the redline into the DPA addendum and Ben will prep the runbook for transfer.

If helpful, I'm available for a 20-min call Monday to finalize procurement asks.

—Naomi
